output.reasoning:
The solution patch touches six files: four production Java files (`RuleDescriptionFileNames.java`, `RuleViolationFileNameStrategyFactory.java`, `StoreIntegrity.java`, and `TextFileBasedViolationStore.java`), one source user-guide file, and its checked-in generated HTML counterpart. There are no unrelated test, build, or configuration edits in the reference solution, and the production change is well above the lane's substantive-scope floor.

The promised behavior traces cleanly through the patch. Initialization parses the exact integrity modes, resolves either the constructor-supplied or configured naming strategy, validates the index before opening it, and performs fail/repair examination while holding the per-canonical-index monitor. Description naming normalizes only CRLF for deterministic built-in derivation, retains an eligible whole ASCII word, appends a stable SHA-256 discriminator, and respects the 200-character/safe-character constraints. Custom strategy loading enforces a public no-argument constructor while permitting a non-public implementation class, and the wrapper invokes custom strategies with the original rule description before normalizing only the returned filename.

Integrity classification gives shared entries precedence, distinguishes broken/resolved/misplaced/colliding/occupied/unowned states, compares symbolic and hard-link file identity, and sorts findings by condition and description/name. Repair mutates only broken, resolved, and safely misplaced entries and writes the index only when mappings change; fail reports without mutation, including the absent-index preflight. Saving is serialized with examination, checks target ownership before inserting a new mapping, protects the index and out-of-folder targets (including aliases), writes known entries through valid links, and implements repair-mode empty-save forgetting while retaining shared files.

The concurrency changes synchronize reloads, reads, mapping changes, repair, and save transactions on the shared `FileSyncedProperties` object, addressing the prior clear/put visibility and preflight-lock concerns. The current dynamic verification passes all 42 baseline tests and all 148 maintenance tests. The repository's visible Java gates include SpotBugs and Spotless unused-import handling; no demonstrable gate violation is present. Documentation source and generated HTML are synchronized and directly relevant. I found no confirmed S1, S2, S3, S4, or S6 defect.
output.summary: Clean, substantive implementation of filename strategies, integrity classification/repair/fail behavior, safe saving, and in-process synchronization, with focused synchronized documentation changes.
